task.name: A catalog entry names an upstream identifier the provider has retired, so a superseded model is selected and priced from a rate card that no longer applies
task.story_text:
## Observed

A model identifier that a provider has retired continues to be offered for routing, and the spend it
records is computed from a rate card the provider has replaced.

Model identity is declared in three places that are maintained by hand and never checked against the
provider: a shipped catalog entry, a canonical-alias map, and an accounting table. All three still
carry an identifier the provider announced for retirement and has since removed from its published
model list. The identifier has not stopped resolving upstream — calls made through it complete with
exit 0 and return token counts — so nothing in the system observes that the name now designates a
different model than the one whose capability, tier and price were recorded against it. The
accounting table's own comments still describe the entry as an alias for a model generation two
releases old.

The consequences are not confined to a stale label:

Spend is misreported in the direction that matters. Two runs on 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-09 each
recorded roughly `$3.7` of estimated cost against ~6.4M input and ~78k output tokens. Priced against
the rate card the provider currently publishes for the model the identifier now resolves to, the same
usage is several times cheaper. The estimate is not marked provisional; it is `cost_provenance:
estimated` like every other estimate, and it feeds budget ceilings, cost-target routing and price
tie-breaks.

The routing declaration no longer describes the model being invoked. The entry is banded as a strong
reasoning model, and it was returned to the reviewer pool on that basis. Every recorded run shows
zero reasoning tokens, and the adapter for this provider passes no request-level control for
reasoning behaviour at all — it forwards a model name and a response format and nothing else. Where
a provider has moved reasoning from a model-name distinction to a request parameter, an identifier
inherited from the old scheme cannot express the mode it was banded for.

The cost model has no place for a rate the provider bills separately. Every recorded run shows zero
cached input tokens, and there is no cached-input rate in the catalog schema for this provider, so a
tier the provider prices roughly two orders of magnitude below its uncached rate is neither requested
nor accounted for.

## Expected

An identifier the system offers for routing is one the provider currently serves, and it designates
the same model whose capability, tier and price were recorded against it. Where a provider retires,
re-points or re-scopes an identifier, that is discoverable from the system's own configuration rather
than from a run whose output happens to look wrong — and discoverable at the point configuration is
loaded, when an operator can still act on it, not after a run has spent against it.

An identifier that silently continues to resolve after it has been retired is the more dangerous case
than one that stops working, because a hard failure is self-announcing and a soft substitution is
not. Where the system cannot establish that a name still means what was recorded about it, that
uncertainty is stated rather than absorbed, and a declaration that cannot be confirmed does not carry
the same weight in selection as one that can.

Recorded cost reflects what the provider actually bills for the invocation that was made. Where a
provider prices a class of input at a distinct rate, the system can express that rate and account for
it, rather than pricing every input at the highest of the provider's rates. A cost figure that is
known to be derived from a rate card that may no longer apply is distinguishable from one that is
not, so a downstream decision made on price can tell how much the price is worth.

Where a provider expresses a behavioural mode as a request parameter rather than as a distinct model
name, the system can express that mode. A role assigned a model for a property that property must be
requested to obtain is invoked in a way that actually requests it.

## Diagnosis

**Observed symptom.** A model routed as a strong reasoning reviewer records zero reasoning tokens,
zero cached input, and an estimated cost several times the provider's published rate — while
completing successfully, so nothing flags it.

**Evidence.**

- `src/theforge/config/data/models.yaml:283-310` — two shipped catalog entries pin identifiers the
  provider has retired, with input/output rates from the superseded rate card and a
  `pricing_provenance` naming the retired identifier as its own source.
- `src/theforge/config/models.py:216-217` — the canonical-alias map resolves the same retired
  identifiers, so a project-level reference to them resolves cleanly rather than failing.
- `src/theforge/runners/schema_utils.py:87-90` — the accounting table carries four entries for this
  provider, two of them commented as aliases of a model generation two releases old, at the same
  superseded rates.
- `forge.yaml:101` — the entry is in `models.enabled`, unbenched 2026-08-08 under #2207, which
  returned it to the reviewer pool.
- `.forge/audits/runs/5fd68935e09b.json` — two review agents, `success: true`, `exit_code: 0`,
  `cost_provenance: estimated`, `$3.727` and `$3.683`; `usage.thinking_tokens: 0` and
  `usage.cache_read_tokens: 0` on both.
- `src/theforge/runners/adapters/deepseek.py:32-47` — the adapter forwards a model name and a
  response format; it passes no reasoning-mode parameter and reads no reasoning-token field.
- Provider's published change log and model list, retrieved 2026-08-09: the identifiers in use are
  absent, superseded by two current identifiers with a different rate card and a separately-billed
  cached-input rate; reasoning is now a request-level toggle rather than a model-name distinction.

**Ruled out.** Not an auth or availability failure: calls complete with exit 0 and real token counts.
Not the missing-accounting-table case of #2335: this identifier is present in the table, so no
cost-unknown warning fires and the wrong price is recorded confidently. Not a per-run anomaly: every
recorded run for this identifier shows the same zero reasoning tokens and zero cached input. Not the
config duplicate-declaration check, which compares project configuration against the shipped catalog
and has no notion of what the provider currently serves.

**Confirmed cause.** Model identity and price are hand-maintained in three code-side locations with
no mechanism that compares them against the provider, and no mechanism that distinguishes an
identifier still served from one that resolves only because the provider is being lenient. A retired
identifier therefore stays selectable indefinitely, carrying declarations that describe a model it no
longer designates, and the failure surfaces only as quiet inaccuracy in cost and capability rather
than as an error.

- **Affected code path:** `theforge.config.data.models` catalog entries, `theforge.config.models`
  canonical-alias map, `theforge.runners.schema_utils.PRICING_TABLE`, and
  `theforge.runners.adapters.deepseek._run_deepseek`.

**Fix-success criterion.** The identifiers offered for this provider are ones it currently serves,
priced from the rate card in force including its separately-billed input tier, with the behavioural
mode the routing declaration claims actually requested at invocation; and a subsequent retirement of
any provider identifier is surfaced from configuration rather than inferred from a run's output.

handoff.summary: Made upstream model identity an explicit, expiring declaration in the catalog schema and stopped the retired DeepSeek identifiers from being routable or priceable. Added an `identity` block (status served|retired, verified_against, verified_on, retired_reason), an `invocation.reasoning_mode` block, and `cost.cached_input_per_mtok` to the one canonical model-definition parser. Retired entries are split out of AGENT_REGISTRY into RETIRED_MODEL_REGISTRY: unroutable, priceless, but still resolvable so a config naming one fails at load with the retirement and its replacement named. Verified DeepSeek's current model list and pricing against api-docs.deepseek.com and replaced deepseek-reasoner/deepseek-chat with deepseek-v4-pro (0.435/0.87, cache-hit 0.003625) and deepseek-v4-flash (0.14/0.28, cache-hit 0.0028). Removed the four DeepSeek rows from PRICING_TABLE and made _estimate_cost resolve rates through a new pricing_for() that reads catalog entries first and falls back to the table; local-endpoint 0.00 figures are excluded so codestral-style entries keep their old behaviour. The OpenAI-compatible adapters now read prompt_cache_hit_tokens / prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens and completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens (splitting reasoning out of completion_tokens so it is not billed twice), and _UsageAccumulator passes accumulated cache reads to the estimator — gated by a new cache_reads_are_subset_of_input() so Anthropic, which reports cache reads alongside an already-exclusive input count, is unaffected. DeepSeek's routing EffortKnob moved from KNOB_NONE to KNOB_EFFORT(captures_thinking_spend=True), reasoning_mode propagates AgentSpec -> ModelInfo -> AgentDef -> ModelProfile (and through apply_model_info on mid-run swaps), and a single deepseek_request_kwargs() helper builds the `thinking` block for the single-shot, tool-loop and finalizer paths alike, mapping forge's low/medium/high onto DeepSeek's low/high/max. forge check-config reports unconfirmed identifiers under a new 'upstream identifier not confirmed' section.

acceptance_criteria.notes: Two mechanisms. (1) A declared retirement is a hard failure at config load naming the reason and the replacement — resolve_agent_spec consults RETIRED_MODEL_REGISTRY before reporting unknown, so the legacy alias spellings reach the explanation too. story_deviations: The plan's Step 3 said to remove the retired DeepSeek names from the alias map. I kept them and pointed them at the now-retired canonical ids instead. Removing them would have degraded the failure for an existing config from 'this identifier was retired, use deepseek-v4-pro' to 'unknown model', which reads as a typo — the opposite of the story's point that a soft substitution is more dangerous than a hard failure because it is not self-announcing.

The plan reviewer suggested marking the entries retired without replacements if current identifiers could not be verified. WebFetch against api-docs.deepseek.com returned the served model list, the full pricing table (cache-hit / cache-miss / output), and the thinking parameter contract, so the replacements are provider-attested rather than guessed.

Step 5's 'provider invocation options on ModelProfile' was implemented as one typed field (reasoning_mode) plus a routing.py change to the existing reasoning-effort axis, rather than a generic options bag — the reviewer's P1 asked for exactly one typed control instead of a field the adapter reads speculatively.

deferred_items: Cost-confidence provenance. The spec's Expected section asks that a cost derived from a rate card that may no longer apply be distinguishable from one that is not. Not implemented: _stamp_api_cost_provenance stamps every derived API cost COST_ESTIMATED, and agent_types.COST_PROVENANCE_VALUES has only provider_reported/estimated/unknown. Adding a fourth value means threading provider+model into that seam and updating AgentResult/ModelUsage, audit rendering and every price consumer. It is not part of the story's fix-success criterion, and the DeepSeek entries this story ships are confirmed, so nothing routable is currently in the state the new value would describe. Worth its own issue.

Verification is a recorded declaration with an expiry, not an automated provider check. There is deliberately no network I/O at AGENT_REGISTRY import time (it is built at module import; implicit fetching there would be a startup dependency on every provider). The expiry window is what keeps a stale declaration from carrying the weight of a fresh one. A generated provider snapshot with fetched-at metadata, as the plan reviewer sketched, would be the next step.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the three P1 findings and the P2, within the approved plan. (1) Retired canonical identities are now reserved in config/model_catalog.resolve_project, the single function both project declaration surfaces pass through — models.custom (load.py:411) and inline models.enabled mappings (load.py:221) — so a project can no longer redeclare deepseek-reasoner with its own routing and cost and put it back into config.models. The retired set is read from a memoized cache in model_catalog populated by load_packaged_catalog_split(), not by importing config.models, which would be the identity/catalog/registry import cycle. (2) DeepSeek's thinking control now travels as extra_body={'thinking': {...}} instead of a top-level thinking= kwarg; verified against installed openai 2.53.0 that Completions.create declares an explicit parameter list with no **kwargs, so the previous shape raised TypeError in the client before any request was sent. reasoning_effort stays nested inside DeepSeek's thinking object rather than mapped onto the SDK's own top-level reasoning_effort, because the two are different fields with different vocabularies (DeepSeek accepts 'max'). (3) LoopTurn gained reasoning_content, the OpenAI-compatible loop adapter now reads msg.reasoning_content instead of discarding it, and AgentLoopManager._append_tool_results stopped hardcoding the assistant message to content=None — it now carries turn.text_output and records reasoning_content on the message. reasoning_content is deliberately NOT replayed into the request; see story_deviations. (4) P2: added COST_ESTIMATED_UNCONFIRMED to agent_types, a rate_card_confirmed(provider, model) resolver in schema_utils, and per-component classification in _stamp_api_cost_provenance (threaded profile.provider through _stamp_api_transport), so an estimate derived from a rate card whose model identity is not currently confirmed is distinguishable from one that is.

story_deviations: P1-3's suggested fix — replay the provider's reasoning_content in the follow-up message history — was NOT implemented as described, and this is a deliberate disagreement rather than an omission. DeepSeek's API reference defines the input assistant `reasoning_content` field as belonging to Chat Prefix Completion: 'Used for the thinking mode in the Chat Prefix Completion feature as the input for the CoT in the last assistant message. When using this feature, the `prefix` parameter must be set to true.' Emitting it on an ordinary tool-loop turn would opt every thinking-mode review into a beta feature (with its own base_url) that it never requested. I could not reach a provider source stating that replay is required for normal multi-turn; the guides/multi_round_chat and guides/function_calling pages both resolve to a generic landing page. What I did instead addresses the substance: capture reasoning_content on the turn so it is no longer discarded, and stop erasing the assistant's own text (content was hardcoded to None), which was a real continuity loss affecting every provider, not just DeepSeek. The translators build outgoing messages from named keys so the field cannot leak into a request, and the constraint is documented at both sites. If the reviewer has a provider source showing replay is required for standard tool loops, this should be revisited — it is a one-line change in _translate_messages_openai_chat.

handoff.summary: This iteration fixes the one surviving P1 — DeepSeek's reasoning_content was not replayed on tool-call continuations — and corrects the reasoning I gave for refusing it in the two previous cycles. The provider's thinking-mode guide distinguishes two cases I had collapsed into one: without tool calls a replayed reasoning_content is ignored, but with tool calls it must participate in context concatenation and be passed back on all subsequent turns or the API returns 400. My earlier citation (the API reference scoping the input field to Chat Prefix Completion) describes a different use of the field; generalising it was the error. Rather than flip a global suppression into a global send, the round-trip is now data-driven: _translate_messages_openai_chat replays whatever reasoning_content the loop message carries, and the loop only carries one when the provider reported one. OpenAI's Chat Completions never returns the field, so OpenAI histories never carry the key and its request bodies are unchanged; DeepSeek returns it on every thinking-mode turn, so its histories round-trip. No provider branch exists in shared code, which is what removes the tension that kept this open. Because both DeepSeek history-replaying call sites use that translator, this fixes the tool loop (adapters/openai.py:355) and the DeepSeek finalizer (finalizers.py:108) together — the finalizer replays the entire history at the end of an out-of-iterations/out-of-time review and would 400 on the same rule. Stale comments carrying the old rationale were removed from LoopTurn (schema_utils), _append_tool_results (api.py) and the translator docstring, and the constraint is now documented in docs/guides/model-reference.md.

findings.description: A models.enabled inline declaration or models.custom entry can declare deepseek-reasoner with routing data, load successfully, and place deepseek/deepseek-reasoner/api back into config.models for selection.

Routed DeepSeek profiles with reasoning enabled build a Chat Completions request containing a top-level thinking keyword, which the installed OpenAI SDK rejects with TypeError before any API request is sent.
When a DeepSeek thinking-mode tool call needs another turn, the follow-up message history contains the assistant tool call but not the provider's reasoning_content.
Estimated cost provenance does not distinguish whether a cost was derived from a verified rate card versus an unconfirmed/possibly stale rate card.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 only adds self-declared verification metadata to model_identity.py/model_catalog.py. AGENT_REGISTRY is constructed by load_packaged_catalog() at import time, and the plan defines neither a provider model-list comparison nor a freshness/expiry rule. Consequently a declaration marked verified can remain verified forever after a subsequent retirement—the original failure mode.
  Suggestion: Specify an authoritative verification design, such as a generated provider snapshot carrying fetched-at/max-age metadata whose staleness makes entries unverified and unroutable, or an explicit load-time provider check with defined authentication and offline behavior. Avoid implicit network I/O during AGENT_REGISTRY module import.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 5 assumes the catalog's provider invocation options will be available on ModelProfile, but Step 1 only changes AgentSpec and its parser. ModelProfile/ModelRef in config/types.py and the ModelInfo, AgentDef, profile, role-derivation, and bridge projections do not carry such options. Additionally, routing.py currently declares DeepSeek as EffortKnob(KNOB_NONE, False), so the existing reasoning-effort path will continue reporting and treating the transport as unsupported.
  Suggestion: Add the complete AgentSpec-to-ModelProfile propagation path to the plan and update routing.py if the existing reasoning-effort axis should drive DeepSeek. Define one typed DeepSeek invocation control rather than leaving the adapter to read a field that never reaches it.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The actual DeepSeek tool-loop path is _run_loop_deepseek() in runners/api.py, which calls _make_openai_chat_adapter() directly; it does not call _make_deepseek_adapter() from deepseek.py. The timeout path in runners/finalizers.py also constructs independent DeepSeek request kwargs. Therefore modifying only deepseek.py/schema_utils.py will not request reasoning mode for normal routed loop calls or finalization, and generic _make_openai_usage() will still discard provider-specific reasoning usage.
  Suggestion: Include runners/api.py, runners/finalizers.py, and the relevant openai.py helper seam. Route every DeepSeek request—single-shot, tool loop, and finalizer—through shared DeepSeek request-option and usage-normalization helpers.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 4 changes the estimator but omits its load-bearing callers. _make_openai_usage() and _openai_result() in runners/adapters/openai.py hardcode cache_read_tokens=0, while _UsageAccumulator.to_model_usage() in runners/api.py accumulates cache_read_tokens but does not pass them as cached_input_tokens to _estimate_cost(). Thus the separately billed cached-input rate would never affect recorded DeepSeek loop costs.
  Suggestion: Plan provider-specific cache-usage extraction for all DeepSeek response paths, pass the accumulated cached-token count from runners/api.py into _estimate_cost(), and cover both single-shot and finalizer usage.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The plan adds catalog pricing/identity provenance but does not change the recorded cost-confidence contract. _stamp_api_cost_provenance() in runners/api.py stamps every non-null derived API cost as 'estimated', and agent_types.py only defines provider_reported, estimated, and unknown. Consequently a cost based on a stale or unverified rate card remains indistinguishable in audits and downstream budget or price decisions.
  Suggestion: Add the cost-confidence/provenance representation and its propagation through AgentResult/ModelUsage, audit rendering, and price consumers, or require unverified pricing to produce cost unknown and be excluded from price-based selection.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 offers 'eliminate stale DeepSeek entries from PRICING_TABLE' as an option, but PRICING_TABLE membership is read outside the listed files: assignment.py:2218-2220 uses (profile.provider_family, profile.model) in PRICING_TABLE as the spend-measurable gate, and runner_claude.py:171-198 indexes it directly. Removing deepseek rows without adding the current identifiers at the same time makes those models cost-unknown, which halts sprints rather than fixing pricing.
  Suggestion: Keep PRICING_TABLE populated for every routable deepseek identifier (or make assignment._is_spend_measurable consult the catalog too, and update it explicitly in the step's file list). Do not leave a window where a routable model has no pricing entry.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 says the new verification fields are optional but also that a model with a 'retired, unverified, or unsupported upstream identifier fails configuration load'. Read literally, every existing entry in models.yaml (which will carry none of the new metadata) is 'unverified' and would fail load.
  Suggestion: Scope the load-time failure to entries whose declared status is explicitly retired/unsupported. Absence of verification metadata should degrade the declaration's weight (per the uncertainty criterion), not break config load for the whole catalog.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 requires 'currently published provider identifiers' and 'current input/output/cached-input rates' but names none, and the spec does not name them either. A dev agent without network access cannot derive these values, and guessing produces a wrong rate card — the exact defect being fixed.
  Suggestion: If the current identifiers/rates cannot be verified against the provider during implementation, mark the existing deepseek entries retired/non-routable with an explicit reason rather than inventing replacements. That still satisfies the routing-safety and load-time-discoverability criteria; the pricing criteria can then be met by the cached-input schema work alone.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 lists forge.yaml. It is skip-worktree in dev worktrees (git ls-files -v forge.yaml → S), so an edit there cannot be delivered by the dev agent; and the deepseek entry at forge.yaml:101 is already commented out (re-benched 2026-08-09), so no edit is needed.
  Suggestion: Drop forge.yaml from Step 2's file list. If an operator-side forge.yaml change is required after the catalog rename, surface it as an operator-action note in the PR body instead.

plan_finding_registry.description: Step 1 only adds self-declared verification metadata to model_identity.py/model_catalog.py. AGENT_REGISTRY is constructed by load_packaged_catalog() at import time, and the plan defines neither a provider model-list comparison nor a freshness/expiry rule. Consequently a declaration marked verified can remain verified forever after a subsequent retirement—the original failure mode.

Step 5 assumes the catalog's provider invocation options will be available on ModelProfile, but Step 1 only changes AgentSpec and its parser. ModelProfile/ModelRef in config/types.py and the ModelInfo, AgentDef, profile, role-derivation, and bridge projections do not carry such options. Additionally, routing.py currently declares DeepSeek as EffortKnob(KNOB_NONE, False), so the existing reasoning-effort path will continue reporting and treating the transport as unsupported.

The actual DeepSeek tool-loop path is _run_loop_deepseek() in runners/api.py, which calls _make_openai_chat_adapter() directly; it does not call _make_deepseek_adapter() from deepseek.py. The timeout path in runners/finalizers.py also constructs independent DeepSeek request kwargs. Therefore modifying only deepseek.py/schema_utils.py will not request reasoning mode for normal routed loop calls or finalization, and generic _make_openai_usage() will still discard provider-specific reasoning usage.

Step 4 changes the estimator but omits its load-bearing callers. _make_openai_usage() and _openai_result() in runners/adapters/openai.py hardcode cache_read_tokens=0, while _UsageAccumulator.to_model_usage() in runners/api.py accumulates cache_read_tokens but does not pass them as cached_input_tokens to _estimate_cost(). Thus the separately billed cached-input rate would never affect recorded DeepSeek loop costs.

The plan adds catalog pricing/identity provenance but does not change the recorded cost-confidence contract. _stamp_api_cost_provenance() in runners/api.py stamps every non-null derived API cost as 'estimated', and agent_types.py only defines provider_reported, estimated, and unknown. Consequently a cost based on a stale or unverified rate card remains indistinguishable in audits and downstream budget or price decisions.

Step 4 offers 'eliminate stale DeepSeek entries from PRICING_TABLE' as an option, but PRICING_TABLE membership is read outside the listed files: assignment.py:2218-2220 uses (profile.provider_family, profile.model) in PRICING_TABLE as the spend-measurable gate, and runner_claude.py:171-198 indexes it directly. Removing deepseek rows without adding the current identifiers at the same time makes those models cost-unknown, which halts sprints rather than fixing pricing.

Step 1 says the new verification fields are optional but also that a model with a 'retired, unverified, or unsupported upstream identifier fails configuration load'. Read literally, every existing entry in models.yaml (which will carry none of the new metadata) is 'unverified' and would fail load.

Step 2 requires 'currently published provider identifiers' and 'current input/output/cached-input rates' but names none, and the spec does not name them either. A dev agent without network access cannot derive these values, and guessing produces a wrong rate card — the exact defect being fixed.

Step 2 lists forge.yaml. It is skip-worktree in dev worktrees (git ls-files -v forge.yaml → S), so an edit there cannot be delivered by the dev agent; and the deepseek entry at forge.yaml:101 is already commented out (re-benched 2026-08-09), so no edit is needed.

DeepSeek is an API transport wrapping the OpenAI runner, so the token parser in _make_openai_usage and the results builder in _openai_result must be updated to inspect the OpenAI/DeepSeek usage detail fields (such as prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens and completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens) to properly extract cache_read_tokens and thinking_tokens respectively.

tests/test_model_catalog.py carries an explicit _SHIPPED_ROUTING dictionary asserting model keys, including the retired DeepSeek identifiers. Updating the default model catalog without updating these assertions will cause test_the_builtin_registry_is_what_the_catalog_data_says to fail.

_thinking_spend_captured in src/theforge/assignment.py checks if (profile.provider_family, profile.model) is present in PRICING_TABLE to decide if the model's run cost actually includes thinking spend. If DeepSeek is removed or updated in PRICING_TABLE, ensure this check correctly uses catalog pricing or handles catalog-based pricing.

findings.description: The Expected section bundles four independent fixes across different subsystems: (1) a general mechanism to verify model identifiers against the provider and surface retirement/re-pointing at config-load time, with unconfirmed declarations weighted down in routing selection; (2) extending the cost-model schema to express a separately-billed cached-input rate and mark cost figures as tied to a possibly-stale rate card; (3) a provider-adapter change (deepseek) to request reasoning mode via a request parameter instead of relying on model-name distinction. These touch distinct code paths (config/catalog validation vs. runners/schema_utils pricing schema vs. runners/adapters/deepseek behavior), have independent success criteria, and could each be reviewed and landed on its own. A single PR covering all three would mix a cross-provider verification mechanism with a provider-specific request-parameter fix and a pricing-schema extension, which is hard to review coherently as one change.

stories.name: Verify provider model identifiers and surface retirement at config load
acs: An identifier offered for routing is confirmed against the provider's currently published model list at the point configuration is loaded, not discovered later from run output.
When a provider has retired, re-pointed, or re-scoped an identifier, that state is reported to the operator at config-load time, before any run spends against it.
A declaration that cannot be confirmed against the provider is weighted lower in routing/reviewer selection than a declaration that can.

stories.name: Support provider-specific cached-input pricing and rate-card provenance
acs: The cost-model schema can express a distinct rate for a provider's cached-input tier, separate from its uncached input rate.
Recorded cost for a run reflects the cached-input rate when cached tokens were used, rather than always pricing input at the uncached rate.
A cost figure derived from a rate card that may no longer match the provider's current pricing is distinguishable from one that is not.

stories.name: Request reasoning mode explicitly for providers that expose it as a request parameter
acs: For a provider where reasoning is a request-level parameter rather than a model-name distinction, a role banded for reasoning behavior is invoked with that parameter set.
A run's recorded reasoning-token usage reflects the mode actually requested, rather than silently returning zero because the mode was never requested.

Routed DeepSeek profiles with reasoning enabled build a Chat Completions request containing a top-level thinking keyword, which the installed OpenAI SDK rejects with TypeError before any API request is sent.

Estimated cost provenance does not distinguish whether a cost was derived from a verified rate card versus an unconfirmed/possibly stale rate card.

plan_structured.approach: Make DeepSeek model identity, pricing, and invocation mode explicit in the existing catalog/parser path, then make the runner cost estimator consume the same catalog data instead of maintaining a separate stale pricing table. Add load-time validation that flags retired or unverified upstream identifiers before routing can select them.

steps.description: Extend model catalog schema for provider verification, cached-input pricing, and request-level reasoning mode
steps.details: Add optional fields to the existing model profile data path for upstream/provider identifier verification metadata, cached input cost per million tokens, and provider-specific invocation options such as reasoning mode. Update catalog parsing validation so a model with a retired, unverified, or unsupported upstream identifier fails configuration load unless explicitly marked non-routable/disabled with a clear reason.

steps.description: Replace retired DeepSeek catalog identifiers and rates with current served identifiers
steps.details: Update shipped DeepSeek entries to use currently published provider identifiers, current input/output/cached-input rates, and accurate pricing/identity provenance. Remove or disable retired DeepSeek identifiers from routable defaults and project enabled models so routing cannot select the retired names.

steps.description: Stop legacy aliases from silently resolving retired DeepSeek identifiers
steps.details: Remove retired DeepSeek names from the canonical alias map or change them to validation failures with an explicit retired-identifier message. Keep only aliases that preserve the same upstream model identity and pricing semantics.

steps.description: Unify cost estimation with catalog pricing and support cached-input rates
steps.details: Eliminate stale DeepSeek entries from PRICING_TABLE or make the estimator prefer catalog-loaded pricing for known model profiles. Add cached-input cost calculation using the explicit cached-input rate when present, falling back to existing generic behavior only for providers without a catalog-specific cached tier.

steps.description: Pass configured DeepSeek reasoning mode through the adapter and capture returned reasoning usage
steps.details: Read the model profile's provider invocation options in the DeepSeek adapter and forward the request-level reasoning mode required by profiles banded as reasoning models. Normalize any provider-reported reasoning token field into the existing usage.thinking_tokens path instead of relying on model name alone.

steps.description: Add focused tests for DeepSeek config validation, routing eligibility, pricing, and adapter parameters
steps.details: Add tests that retired DeepSeek identifiers fail or are excluded at configuration load, current identifiers load with cached-input pricing, legacy aliases no longer mask retired names, cost estimation uses cached-input rates, and the DeepSeek adapter forwards the configured reasoning-mode parameter without invoking real provider CLIs.

criteria_mapping.criterion: An identifier the system offers for routing is one the provider currently serves, and it designates the same model whose capability, tier and price were recorded against it.
Where a provider retires, re-points or re-scopes an identifier, that is discoverable from the system's own configuration at load time.

Where the system cannot establish that a name still means what was recorded about it, that uncertainty is stated rather than absorbed, and a declaration that cannot be confirmed does not carry the same weight in selection as one that can.
Recorded cost reflects what the provider actually bills for the invocation that was made, including separately billed input tiers.
A cost figure derived from a rate card that may no longer apply is distinguishable from one that is not.
Where a provider expresses a behavioural mode as a request parameter rather than as a distinct model name, the system can express that mode.
A role assigned a model for a property that property must be requested to obtain is invoked in a way that actually requests it.
